landmarks.name: Grain Elevator (Elevator)
landmarks.what: Massive reinforced-concrete grain silo complex (built 1940) in the Voroshilovsky district, south of the Tsaritsa; still standing today (Wikidata Q16721871).
landmarks.battle_role: Fortress-like strongpoint 14-22 Sept 1942: ~50 Soviet defenders (elements of 35th Guards RD and 92nd Naval Rifle Bde) held it against German 94th ID / 29th Motorized for a week without water or resupply; it dominated the flat southern city and appeared on the planned German 'Stalingrad shield' badge. German-held from ~22 Sept until the Jan 1943 collapse.

landmarks.name: Univermag department store (Paulus HQ)
landmarks.what: Central Department Store on Fallen Fighters' Square (Ploshchad Pavshikh Bortsov), city centre. The basement now houses the 'Pamyat' (Memory) museum at 48.7087, 44.5168.
landmarks.battle_role: Fell to German 71st ID in the mid-Sept centre fighting; in Jan 1943 the basement became the final HQ of 6th Army. Field Marshal Paulus was captured here on 31 Jan 1943 by 38th Motorized Rifle Bde troops.

landmarks.name: Mamayev Kurgan (Height 102.0)
landmarks.what: Tatar burial-mound hill between the city centre and the factory district; today crowned by The Motherland Calls statue (48.7425, 44.5369).
landmarks.battle_role: THE key observation point — whoever held it could direct fire onto the Volga crossings and most of the city. Changed hands repeatedly from 13 Sept 1942; from late Sept Batyuk's 284th Rifle Div held the eastern slope, Germans (295th ID) the western; the summit water tanks were a corpse-choked no-man's-land right through November until Jan 1943.

landmarks.name: Stalingrad-1 Main Railway Station (Volgograd I)
landmarks.what: Main passenger terminus, ~700 m west of the Volga in the city centre (ru-Wikipedia coords).
landmarks.battle_role: Epicentre of the 14-19 Sept 1942 centre battle — changed hands over a dozen times; the 1st Bn, 42nd Gds Regt of Rodimtsev's 13th Guards was destroyed defending it. Firmly German (71st ID, LI Corps) from ~20 Sept until the southern-pocket surrender 31 Jan 1943.

landmarks.name: Stalingrad-2 Railway Station (Volgograd II)
landmarks.what: Secondary passenger/freight station in the southern city, ~700 m NW of the Grain Elevator (ru-Wikipedia coords).
landmarks.battle_role: Axis of the German 29th Motorized / 94th ID drive of 15-22 Sept that isolated the Grain Elevator; in German hands from mid-Sept, rear-area/rail unloading zone of the southern city thereafter.

landmarks.name: Barrikady Gun Factory (Ordnance Factory No. 221)
landmarks.what: Artillery factory (naval/heavy gun barrels) in the northern factory district; modern FNPTs 'Titan-Barrikady' industrial polygon (OSM way 99192963, centroid given).
landmarks.battle_role: Main German objective of the 14 Oct - 18 Nov assaults (305th and 389th ID plus pioneer battalions). By Operation Hubertus (9-12 Nov) the Germans held virtually the whole plant; Lyudnikov's 138th Rifle Div was pinned in a 700x400 m riverbank strip behind it ('Lyudnikov's Island' — memorial front-line marker verified at 48.7733, 44.5865).

landmarks.name: Krasny Oktyabr (Red October) Steel Works
landmarks.what: Metallurgical plant (quality steel) between Barrikady and Mamayev Kurgan; still an operating steel works (OSM industrial polygon way 299389945, centroid given).
landmarks.battle_role: Defended hall-by-hall by Guriev's 39th Guards RD from mid-Oct; German 79th ID took most workshops by early Nov but the open-hearth (Martin) shop's eastern half stayed Soviet. The front froze mid-plant on 11-18 Nov and never moved again until the Soviet counterattacks.

landmarks.name: Dzerzhinsky Tractor Factory (STZ)
landmarks.what: Stalingrad Tractor Factory, northernmost of the three giant plants (OSM: Волгоградский тракторный завод; en-Wikipedia plant coord 48.8002, 44.6103; Dzerzhinsky Square gate at 48.8019, 44.6053).
landmarks.battle_role: Built/repaired T-34s during the battle itself, crews sometimes driving unpainted tanks straight into action; workers' militia fought on 23 Aug when 16th Pz reached the Volga just north. Stormed 14-17 Oct 1942 by 14th Pz, 305th and 389th ID — the Germans took the plant and reached the Volga behind it, splitting 62nd Army in two. German-held at the time of Uranus.

landmarks.name: Gerhardt's Mill (Grudinin's Mill)
landmarks.what: Brick steam flour mill (1903), ~350 m from the Volga bank; deliberately preserved as a ruin beside today's Panorama Museum.
landmarks.battle_role: Fortified strongpoint and forward command post of 42nd Gds Regt (13th Guards) from 14 Sept 1942 to the end — the hard anchor of the central Soviet bridgehead, covering the 62nd Army crossing and Pavlov's House 250 m NW.

landmarks.name: Pavlov's House
landmarks.what: Four-storey apartment block on 9 January Square (now Lenin Square), rebuilt after the war with a memorial colonnade wall.
landmarks.battle_role: Held for ~58 days (27 Sept - 24 Nov 1942) by Sgt Yakov Pavlov's / Lt Afanasyev's ~25-man garrison of 13th Guards; its fields of fire over the square made it the NW cornerstone of the central bridgehead. Still Soviet-held, ~300 m from German lines, at the moment of Uranus.

landmarks.name: Central ferry crossing (62nd Army crossing)
landmarks.what: The main central landing stage on the right bank (today's central embankment — officially 'Embankment of the 62nd Army' — by the river station, OSM stop at 48.7024, 44.5209), fed from Krasnaya Sloboda on the left bank.
landmarks.battle_role: Lifeline of 62nd Army: 13th Guards crossed here under fire 14-15 Sept 1942. From late Sept it lay under direct machine-gun and artillery fire once the Germans reached the bank south of the bridgehead, and traffic shifted north to the factory-district crossings (Crossing 62) and Zaytsevsky Island footbridges. At Uranus the landing stage itself was on the German side of the line.

landmarks.name: Tsaritsa river gully
landmarks.what: Deep ravine of the (now largely culverted) Tsaritsa stream, mouth at the Volga ≈48.699, 44.525-526, running WNW through the city (open upstream OSM stream segments at 48.7099, 44.4830 → 48.7147, 44.4642); it divides the city centre from the southern districts.
landmarks.battle_role: Corps boundary and assault axis: German 71st ID attacked north of it, 94th ID/29th Mot south of it in Sept 1942. Chuikov's first city HQ ('Tsaritsyn bunker') was dug into the gully near the mouth until abandoned mid-Sept. Entirely behind German lines from ~27 Sept until Jan 1943.

frontline_nov1942: On 18-19 Nov 1942 (eve/moment of Uranus) the Germans held roughly 90% of the ruined city; Chuikov's 62nd Army was compressed into THREE separated slivers on the west bank, nowhere much more than 500 m deep. From north to south: (1) The Rynok-Spartanovka pocket (Group Gorokhov: 124th/149th Bdes) around 48.820N 44.630E to 48.821N 44.634E, north of the Mokraya Mechetka stream — cut off from the rest of the army since the Germans took the Tractor Factory. (2) The Dzerzhinsky Tractor Factory (48.794N 44.603E) was entirely German since 14-17 Oct, with 14th Pz/389th ID holding the Volga bank behind it — the first place 6th Army split the 62nd Army on the river. (3) 'Lyudnikov's Island': the 138th Rifle Div's ~700x400 m strip on the bank behind the Barrikady factory, front-edge memorial marker at 48.7733N 44.5865E — isolated on 11 Nov when Operation Hubertus (305th/389th ID + pioneer battalions) reached the Volga on both flanks; the Barrikady plant itself (48.777N 44.584E) was German. (4) At Red October (48.752N 44.562E) German 79th ID held most workshops but 39th Gds RD kept the eastern half of the open-hearth shop and the bank strip (~48.755-48.767N, 44.565-44.575E); the line ran through the middle of the plant. (5) Over Mamayev Kurgan (48.7425N 44.537E) the front crossed the hill: 284th RD (Batyuk) on the eastern slope, 295th ID on the west, the summit water tanks no-man's-land. (6) The 13th Guards' central bridgehead, 200-500 m deep, ran from Mamayev's SE base along the bank through Pavlov's House (48.7160N 44.5315E) and Gerhardt's Mill (48.7155N 44.5329E); Germans held the Main Station (48.7125N 44.5136E), Univermag (48.7086N 44.5165E) and had stood on the Volga bank between the bridgehead's southern edge and the Tsaritsa since ~27 Sept, so the central ferry landing (48.7065N 44.5238E) was behind German lines. (7) Everything south of the Tsaritsa gully (mouth 48.699N 44.525E) — Stalingrad-2 station (48.6925N 44.4811E) and the Grain Elevator (48.6880N 44.4827E) — was German since ~22-27 Sept. (8) The German-held city strip ended at Kuporosnoye (~48.635N 44.50E), where the 64th Army's lines began. Net: a continuous German corridor to the Volga from Latoshinka to the Tsaritsa mouth, interrupted only by the three Soviet bridgeheads; Uranus (19-23 Nov) broke through NOT here but over the Don at Kletskaya/Serafimovich and south of Beketovka, closing the ring at Kalach on 23 Nov and freezing this city frontline in place.
imagery_source: Sentinel-2 L2A winter scene pair of 2024-01-17 (orbit-synchronous tiles 38UMV + 38UMU), Copernicus/ESA via the AWS 'sentinel-cogs' open bucket (earth-search STAC, no auth). Primary tile S2B_38UMV_20240117_0_L2A: 6.5% cloud, 92.7% snow cover — full snowpack with the unfrozen Volga reading near-black. TCI (true-colour RGB, 10 m) COG verified HTTP 200: https://sentinel-cogs.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/sentinel-s2-l2a-cogs/38/U/MV/2024/1/S2B_38UMV_20240117_0_L2A/TCI.tif (34 MB; southern companion .../38/U/MU/2024/1/S2B_38UMU_20240117_0_L2A/TCI.tif also 200). STAC item: https://earth-search.aws.element84.com/v1/collections/sentinel-2-l2a/items/S2B_38UMV_20240117_0_L2A. Alternative cleaner-sky southern tile: S2B_38UMU_20240216_0_L2A (2.0% cloud, 97% snow) but its north edge (48.753N) cuts off Barrikady and the Tractor Factory, hence the same-day 2024-01-17 mosaic. A 10 m city crop (44.30-44.75E, 48.60-48.90N, 3329x3356 px) was mosaicked and downloaded; visually confirmed snowbound with all battle landmarks in frame.
notes: Verification method: every listed URL was checked live (curl -I/-o with status codes, LOC via its JSON API + IIIF because its HTML fronts a bot-blocking WAF: loc.gov HTML pages 403 to curl/WebFetch from this network but https://www.loc.gov/item/2002624030/?fo=json and tile.loc.gov IIIF both return 200 — cite the item URL for humans, use the IIIF URL for downloads). Landmark coordinates were cross-verified against modern Volgograd geography via en/ru Wikipedia coordinate APIs, Wikidata (grain elevator Q16721871), OSM Nominatim and Overpass (factory landuse polygons, Lyudnikov memorial marker); all lie consistently along the west-bank city strip of the 100 km DEM (centre 48.708N 44.513E → UTM 38N easting ~463 km). Caveats: (1) pamyat-naroda.ru (Russian MoD archive with genuine scanned 62nd Army combat maps) answers 200 on its front page but 401 on /ops/ subpages from this network — likely geo/anti-bot gating; treat as browse-by-hand source, no verified deep link included. (2) Mapster (igrek.amzp.pl) has no Stalingrad coverage (Poland/Central Europe only) — the German 1:25k/1:20k needs are covered instead by the LOC Stalingrad-Süd sheet and the Rumsey Stadtplan. (3) Best print references for block-level frontlines, if you want more than the verified Commons scans: David Glantz & Jonathan House, 'Armageddon in Stalingrad' (vol. 2 of the Stalingrad Trilogy) + Glantz's 'Companion' volumes (hundreds of daily situation maps redrawn from 6th Army and 62nd Army records), and Jason Mark's 'Island of Fire' (Barrikady) and 'Death of the Leaping Horseman' — the Commons Barrikady/Roter Oktober/Mitte scans above are derived from that material. (4) For georeferencing the 1942 Stadtplan onto the DEM, EtoMesto's overlay (already georeferenced) is the fastest path — its calibration can be sanity-checked against the verified landmark coordinates. (5) The downloaded winter GeoTIFF is EPSG:32638 (UTM 38N), 10 m/px, upper-left (448390, 5416580) — same datum family as the DEM crop, ready for direct alignment.
